create.title: The exact q=8 hard actual-vector mode is a fragmented four-cycle cross-projection
create.statement_tex: On the literal canonical first-band M1 hard complement, restrict to class moduli M=8N with N odd and A congruent to B_2 congruent to V congruent to 2 modulo 8. Exact CRT gives (mathfrak T_M/M^2)=(c_8(u)/8)(mathfrak T_N/N^2), with c_8(u)/8=1/2 for 8|u, -1/2 for u=4 mod 8, and 0 otherwise; this is independent of whether K is a unit. The global u=0 owner deletes only u=0, so nonzero u in both surviving branches and nonzero modulus multiples remain. The canonical normalization is M^(-5)mathfrak T_M=M^(-3)(mathfrak T_M/M^2); after opening the odd trace the four shared local bases contribute exactly 4/M^4=2^(-10)N^(-4). On the local order-four orbit, the literal four actual rows give sum_j F_j overline(G_(j-1))=(1/4)sum_(k mod 4)e_4(k)Fhat_k overline(Ghat_k). Generic hard odd-cofactor labels therefore give a cross-projection. The only structural alignment B_(2,N)=A_N, V_N=0 makes G=F and yields a difference of squares, but the two physical pair labels then coalesce modulo 2N, so R_*=4<=rho_* and the slice is already in the Round-88 coarse owner. Thus the exact q=8 hard survivor is the scalar C_8(U) consisting of the remaining cross-projections, odd completed trace, all four I_b rows, entry/exit, stars, aliases, reflections, and conductor sum before absolute value. Its target |C_8(U)|<<_epsilon X^epsilon(U/B)J^(14/5) remains open. The result is exact only for v_2(M)=3 and supplies neither a J^(-1/6) gain nor a global actual-vector lower bound.
create.next_action: Estimate the scalar q=8 cross-projection across odd-cofactor labels and conductor rows, and separately retain higher two-parts and complementary local modes. Do not replace it by the prior-owned aligned square or by a uniform local trace norm.

update.next_action: Prove cancellation in the exact q=8 odd-cofactor/conductor cross-projection and in the complementary higher-two-part and noncoherent modes. The aligned square is already owned and local trace magnitude gives no fixed-vector estimate.
Close the fixed actual-vector directional estimate, now retaining the exact q=8 cross-projection scalar and all complementary modes. No local projector alone supplies the required top J^(-1/6).
Use q=8 only through the exact fragmented cross-projection control. Do not infer a global lower bound, positive hard eigenspace, or new trace-moment saving.
Treat the residual q=8 fibre through its generic cross-projection, not through further cellwise degree peeling. The only aligned square has R_*=4 and is already coarse-owned.

reject.reason: The local eigenvalue is only the constant c_8(u)/8, while the literal hard coefficient is an odd-cofactor and conductor cross-projection that may vanish or cancel.
The alignment forcing G=F makes the two physical pair labels coincide modulo 2N, hence R_*=4 and the slice is already owned by the Round-88 coarse package.
The owner removes only the integer label u=0; nonzero u congruent to 0 or 4 modulo 8 remain, including nonzero modulus multiples.
When v_2(M)>3, 8 is not coprime to M/8; the full 2-power phase and longer orbit must be retained before CRT with the odd part.
Backtracking words survive in ordinary trace moments, but a fixed-vector coefficient contains separate overlaps with the two rank-one directions and may vanish or cancel.

no_change.reason: The exact q=8 component is reduced to a smaller scalar cross-projection, but no target-scale bound is proved.
Complementary local modes and the unbounded q=8 scalar remain open.
The canonical packet is only one alternative global-route child and no blockwise M1 parent is closed.
Round 100 is confined to one M1 coherent subfamily.
No real-X endpoint or all-denominator estimate is proved.
Neither M9-M1 nor M9-M2 is closed.
No pointwise bound or exponent is improved.

round_assessment.reason: Round 100 converts the q=8 coherent control into the exact fixed-row cross-projection, proves that the only square is prior-owned, and isolates a smaller scalar survivor. It proves no power saving.
